note: P17's oracle: the timebase arithmetic of chapter 17, which is the part of that chapter needing no peripheral. It serves three of its acceptance criteria: the instrument's own cost subtracted visibly, the first run kept apart from the median of the remainder, and the timebase substitution with each wrap period stated. Criterion 1, the byte-identical harness over four bus reads, needs the shield and is not here. Everything is integer arithmetic on counter values and is compared exactly.

elapsed.why: a 32-bit counter counting up, no wrap
a 32-bit counter counting up, across its wrap
SysTick, 24 bits counting down, a hundred ticks
SysTick across its wrap, which is where a 24-bit mask earns its keep
a 24-bit counter counting up, across its wrap
THE SAME PAIR OF READINGS TAKEN AS AN UP COUNTER, which is what step 8's struct can express: a hundred ticks of a down counter read as 16777116 of an up one, nearly a whole wrap

elapsed_refusals.why: a direction that is neither up nor down
a reading that does not fit the stated width, which is a reading from a different counter or a width that is wrong
the same on the second reading

wraps.why: the cycle counter: 32 bits at the core clock, which step 8 states as about 15.3 seconds
a general timer: 32 bits at 1 MHz, stated as about 71.6 minutes
SysTick: 24 bits at the core clock, stated as about 60 milliseconds

wrap_refusals.why: AN INFINITE TICK FREQUENCY, which an earlier !(hz > 0.0) accepted and which gives a wrap period of zero nanoseconds: a plausible number from an impossible input
a tick frequency that is not a number, which the obvious rewrite to hz <= 0.0 would have accepted

subtractions.why: an ordinary reading, the instrument's cost taken off
an interval exactly the instrument's own cost, which is zero work and not an error

subtraction_refusals.why: AN INTERVAL BELOW THE CALIBRATED INSTRUMENT COST, which step 6's subtraction turns into a number near two to the thirty-second rather than into an error
one tick below it, which is the smallest version of the same thing

reports.why: a cold first run and three warm ones, which is the shape step 6 asks to be reported as two numbers
an even number of warm runs, so the median is the mean of the two middle values
two samples, the fewest that have a first run and a remainder
a warm run slower than the cold one, because a first run is not always the slowest and the two are reported apart rather than assumed ordered

report_refusals.why: one sample, which has no remainder to take a median of
more samples than the bound holds
